sdlc_incident_management_best_practices.overview: Best practices for effective SDLC incident management using Bob with ServiceNow, Ansible, and Terraform integration.

principle.name: Document Everything
principle.description: Maintain complete audit trail throughout incident lifecycle
principle.rationale: Provides accountability, enables learning, and supports compliance
principle.implementation: - Update incident tracking (ServiceNow or local markdown) after each major step - Include diagnostic findings in work notes or documentation - Document remediation actions taken - Record verification results - If ServiceNow unavailable, maintain local documentation for later entry

principle.name: Diagnose Before Acting
principle.description: Always run diagnostics before attempting fixes
principle.rationale: Prevents making problems worse and ensures correct remediation
principle.implementation: - Run health checks first - Analyze logs and metrics - Identify root cause before remediation - Document findings

principle.name: Verify Resolution
principle.description: Always confirm the issue is resolved before closing
principle.rationale: Prevents premature closure and recurring incidents
principle.implementation: - Re-run health checks after fixes - Compare before/after metrics - Test affected functionality - Get user confirmation when appropriate

principle.name: Communicate Clearly
principle.description: Keep stakeholders informed throughout the process
principle.implementation: - Explain what you're doing before each step - Show results clearly - Highlight key findings - Provide regular status updates

practice.name: Gather Complete Information
practice.description: Collect all relevant details before creating incident

practice.name: Use Appropriate Urgency/Impact
practice.description: Set correct priority levels for incident tracking

guidelines.urgency: Critical - System down, major business impact
Medium - Minor impact, can wait for scheduled maintenance
guidelines.impact: Affects multiple users or critical systems
Affects single user or non-critical system

practice.note: These levels apply whether using ServiceNow or manual tracking

practice.name: Select Right Remediation Approach
practice.description: Choose appropriate automation based on incident type

incident_type.diagnostic: 1. Check /api/admin/metrics endpoint for server load indicators 2. Run health-check.yml for response times and service status
incident_type.remediation: fix-performance.yml (if artificial delay) OR infrastructure scaling (if overload)
incident_type.note: Always check metrics first to determine if performance issue is due to server overload

incident_type.diagnostic: 1. CRITICAL: Check /api/admin/metrics endpoint first - Look for: cpuUsage, memoryUsage, requestsPerSecond, overloaded flag - High values (>80%) indicate capacity issues 2. Run health-check.yml to confirm slow response times 3. Correlate metrics with performance to confirm root cause
incident_type.remediation: Terraform horizontal scaling + Nginx load balancer
incident_type.critical_requirement: BOTH scaling AND load balancer are required - scaling alone is incomplete

steps.step: 1. Check metrics endpoint: curl -s http://localhost:5001/api/admin/metrics | jq
3. Configure Nginx load balancer for traffic distribution
4. Verify load distribution across all instances
5. Re-check metrics to confirm load is normalized

practice.name: Handle Errors Gracefully
practice.description: When automation fails, have fallback approaches

approaches.approach: Try manual commands if playbook fails
Check logs for detailed error information
Document the issue and escalate if needed

tool.name: ServiceNow MCP
tool.best_practice: Always capture and save the incident number immediately after creation
Update incidents with work notes, not just state changes
Use appropriate state transitions (New → In Progress → Resolved)
Include timestamps and metrics in work notes
NEVER automatically proceed when ServiceNow connection fails - always present options to user

connection_failure_handling.rule: Stop immediately when connection error occurs
Present user with clear options using ask_followup_question
Explain possible causes (credentials, network, instance availability)
Offer to proceed with manual tracking if user chooses
Never assume user wants to continue without ServiceNow

manual_tracking_mode.when: User explicitly chooses to proceed without ServiceNow

implementation.document_all_actions: Append each phase's findings to the markdown file
implementation.provide_summary: At closure, provide formatted summary for manual ServiceNow entry

tool.common_pitfall: Forgetting to update ServiceNow during long troubleshooting sessions
Automatically proceeding without ServiceNow when connection fails (NEVER DO THIS)

tool.name: Ansible MCP
tool.best_practice: Always explain what a playbook does before running it
Review playbook output for errors or warnings
Use check mode (--check) for dry runs when appropriate
Verify inventory and connectivity before running playbooks
tool.common_pitfall: Running remediation playbooks without diagnosing first

tool.name: Terraform MCP
tool.best_practice: Use terraform plan before apply to preview changes
Review state before making infrastructure changes
Have rollback plan before major changes
Always use ABSOLUTE paths for working_dir — relative paths resolve from the MCP server's process directory, not the workspace
After a timed-out apply, always run terraform_show to check if the apply actually completed before retrying
tool.common_pitfall: Making infrastructure changes without understanding impact
Using plan_file to pass raw CLI flags like -replace — plan_file only accepts a saved plan file path. Use Ansible run_adhoc shell module as fallback for unsupported flags.
Retrying terraform apply when a stale state lock is present without first running force-unlock. Use: ansible run_adhoc shell "cd [tf-dir] && terraform force-unlock -force [LOCK_ID]"
Adding new Terraform providers (e.g., hashicorp/local) without running terraform init -upgrade first. The lock file must be updated before apply will succeed.

tool.name: execute_command
tool.best_practice: Use for quick diagnostics and verification
Show command output to user for transparency
Explain what command does before running it

practice.name: Explain Before Execute
practice.description: Always explain what you're about to do

examples.good: "I'll run the health check playbook to diagnose the performance issue. This will check all services and measure response times."

practice.name: Show Results Clearly
practice.description: Display outputs and highlight key information

practice.name: Provide Context
practice.description: Help user understand why actions are needed

examples.good: "The health check shows the backend is responding slowly (3.2s). This indicates a performance bottleneck that needs investigation."

practice.name: Ask for Confirmation
practice.description: Get approval before potentially disruptive actions

stage.name: Creation
stage.best_practice: Gather complete information before creating incident
Set appropriate urgency and impact levels
Add detailed description with symptoms and context

stage.name: Diagnosis
stage.best_practice: Run health checks before detailed investigation
Document findings in ServiceNow work notes

stage.name: Remediation
stage.best_practice: Explain the fix before applying it
For user overload: ALWAYS include load balancer with scaling

stage.name: Closure
stage.best_practice: Include root cause and actions taken

pitfall.issue: Skipping diagnosis and jumping to fixes
pitfall.consequence: May fix wrong problem or make it worse
pitfall.solution: Always diagnose first, even if cause seems obvious

pitfall.consequence: Lost audit trail, difficult to learn from incidents
pitfall.solution: Update ServiceNow after each major step

pitfall.issue: Using wrong playbook for incident type
pitfall.solution: Match playbook to incident type, check available playbooks first
Explain what you're doing and why before each step

pitfall.issue: Scaling backend without load balancer for user overload
pitfall.consequence: Traffic not distributed, overload persists on single instance
pitfall.solution: ALWAYS add load balancer when scaling - both components are required

success_metrics.metric: Root cause identified through systematic diagnosis
User informed and satisfied with resolution

continuous_improvement.practice: Review closed incidents to identify patterns
Update playbooks based on lessons learned
Document new incident types and solutions
Share knowledge with team through ServiceNow notes
